goal: Reduce first-token latency for the interactive workload, preserving the full generation workload and the source correctness checks.
entrypoint: qwen_inference.py::infer (source reference), executed one invocation per call by adapter.run; adapter entry module adapter.py
completion: One run() performs exactly the source's infer(model, inputs, new_tokens=32) for the interactive workload: under torch.inference_mode, CUDA synchronize then t0, BF16 SDPA prefill forward over the batch=1, 256-token GPU-resident prompt (use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1), argmax of the last-position logits as the first token, explicit torch.cuda.synchronize at the first-token-ready boundary then t1 (ttft_ms = (t1-t0)/1e6, the frozen objective; model-execution latency, no queuing/network), then new_tokens-1 = 31 KV-cached greedy decode steps each feeding its argmax token back, final torch.cat of the 32 generated tokens and a closing synchronize before t2. The workload is complete only when all 32 tokens exist (EOS early stop disabled by the explicit loop); the objective scores just the internal first-token boundary while the full generation remains inside run().
state_protocol: prepare(context, request): applies common.configure() numerics (torch.manual_seed(20261020), TF32 off for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark off, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', 4 torch threads / 1 interop), sets the CUDA device from context['device'], loads AutoTokenizer and Qwen3ForCausalLM (dtype=bfloat16, attn_implementation='sdpa', local_files_only=True) from request['assets']['assets'] onto that device in eval mode, reads batch/prompt_tokens/new_tokens from request['workload'], and builds the exact source input (chat template with enable_thinking=False, add_generation_prompt=True; encode add_special_tokens=False; repeat/truncate to prompt_tokens; replicate batch times) as a GPU tensor kept in state. Model loading, tokenization and host input construction are outside timed execution. reset(state): no-op for caches by design - each run() creates its own fresh KV cache inside the timed invocation exactly as the source's first prefill forward does, and weights are never mutated - it only re-seeds torch.manual_seed(20261020) and drops the last result; the process group is untouched. run(state): the full frozen generation described under completion, returning generated tokens, optional per-step last-token logits, and the (t0, t1, t2) nanosecond timings. observe(state, result): detached CPU copies of input_ids, the 32 greedy token ids and, in quality mode, the stacked per-step last-token logits [batch, new_tokens, vocab]; never timings or counters. metrics(state, result, elapsed_ms): ttft_ms, decode_ms, end_to_end_ms, decode_tokens_per_second, generated_tokens_per_second from the source's internal completion boundaries, plus wall-clock derived throughput and torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() queried outside timing (framework resets peak stats immediately before its timer). models(state): {'model': <loaded Qwen3ForCausalLM>}. set_mode(state, mode): 'quality' retains per-step logits (the source capture path used for its reference); 'measure'/'profile' use the source's clean non-capture timing path; forward work is identical.
invariants: Pretrained Qwen3-4B weights loaded from the frozen assets path with dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation='sdpa', local_files_only=True, .eval(); no weight modification, fine-tuning or second reference model on GPU.

Numerical policy from common.configure(): torch.manual_seed(20261020), torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), torch.set_num_threads(4), torch.set_num_interop_threads(1).

Whole generation executes under @torch.inference_mode() with greedy argmax decoding over the last-position logits; logits_to_keep=1 and use_cache=True on every forward, KV cache threaded through the decode loop.

Input construction is exact: workloads.json qwen_inference.prompt rendered with the chat template (enable_thinking=False, add_generation_prompt=True), encoded without special tokens, repeated/truncated to exactly prompt_tokens=256, replicated to batch=1, resident on the context device before timing.
Exactly new_tokens=32 tokens are generated per invocation; EOS early stopping is disabled by the explicit decode loop.

The KV cache is created fresh inside the timed run() (by the prefill forward), never pre-built or pre-warmed in reset(); source-local references (output, cache, generated, logits) stay live through the measured region.

ttft_ms uses the source's internal boundary: sync -> t0, prefill forward + first-token argmax -> explicit 'first-token-ready' torch.cuda.synchronize -> t1; the remaining 31 decode steps and final synchronize still execute inside run().

Correctness scope is reference fidelity only: generated tokens must equal the reference greedy sequence (torch.equal), per-step last-token logits must satisfy assert_close at atol=rtol=0.02, and a +1-corrupted logits negative control must be rejected; no broader accuracy or convergence claim.
Workload dimensions (batch, prompt_tokens, new_tokens) are read from request['workload'] in prepare(), not embedded as constants; the frozen values here are batch=1, prompt_tokens=256, new_tokens=32.
Correctness observations contain only tensors/scalars (input_ids, tokens, per-step logits), never elapsed times or performance counters.
Observations are returned as detached tensors (CPU copies), not hashes or sampled subsets; the framework stores references on CPU.
assumptions: The frozen prompt text is task data read from workloads.json; the adapter locates it next to the module (inputs/source/workloads.json or request['source_root']), with the identical literal string as a last-resort fallback, so input ids match the source byte-for-byte.

Default mode after prepare is 'quality' (full observations available if set_mode is never called); set_mode('measure'/'profile') switches run() to the source's clean non-capture timing path - capture only retains already-computed logits slices and the final stack, it does not change forward work.

peak_allocated_bytes in metrics() reads torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() outside the timer, matching the source's per-sample metric given the framework resets peak stats immediately before its run timer.

The source's reference construction (capture run plus teacher-forced re-run), close/negative checks, warmup=2/repeats=5 loop, reference .pt saving and optional profiling are measurement infrastructure performed by the framework; adapter.run() performs exactly one infer-equivalent invocation.

decode_tokens_per_second (the second goal declared for this interactive row) is exposed as an additional metric using the source's own definition: batch*(new_tokens-1)/decode window, decode window measured between the first-token-ready and final synchronizes.

The offline (batch=8) row and the held-out long_prompt row are separate source goals/cases outside this frozen request; the adapter is dimension-parametric via request['workload'] so a validated variant can reuse it unchanged.
Single-GPU non-distributed task: no process group is created or destroyed by the adapter, and context['device'] is used for all placements instead of .cuda() defaults.

kernel_optimizer.project.discovery.phase is not present in the inspected worker environment, so the optional prefill/decode phase annotations are guarded no-ops; if the API exists in the measured worker they activate automatically.

The leading and trailing torch.cuda.synchronize() calls of infer() are kept inside run() because the source defines its timing window around them and requires the internal first-token-ready synchronize for the ttft_ms objective; they are idempotent with the framework's own boundary syncs.
No sampling or speculative decoding is introduced; decoding remains pure greedy argmax so token-level equality with the reference is reproducible across workers via the fixed seed and frozen weights.
